title: What is an AI receptionist? How it works and what it can’t do
summary: An AI receptionist answers business calls using speech recognition, identifies what the caller needs, and takes action. Here’s how it works on a real call, and where it still falls short.
body_markdown:
An AI receptionist can help pick up your business calls 24/7. It uses speech recognition and natural language processing to answer questions, send texts, and record calls.


Most AI receptionists answer forwarded calls from your phone number or are embedded in the phone system you already use. They also offer features like multilingual support or WhatsApp integration.


This article explains more about what an AI receptionist is, what it can and cannot do, and why it’s worth it for growing small businesses.


##


What an AI receptionist is


An AI receptionist is a software that answers calls autonomously without human help. But contrary to popular belief, it’s not a[phone menu](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-menu/) or a human answering service.


An IVR phone menu, for example, offers fixed options, like “Press one for Sales.” Human answering services outsource agents to answer calls for your business, but they don’t offer the same scalability as AI.


Read our guide to learn[what a virtual receptionist is](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-receptionist/) and get a full breakdown.


##


How an AI receptionist handles a call


Let’s say you’re a home services company offering plumbing and electrical work. A customer calls your number after hours on a Saturday to request an emergency water heater repair. Ordinarily, they’d go to voicemail. But your AI receptionist offers 24/7 availability.


Your AI receptionist can assist the caller by:


- Answering questions based on the knowledge base you provided
- Collecting caller details and syncing them to a CRM, like HubSpot
- Transferring the call to another number if it meets the conditions you set
- Taking action, like texting the caller a booking link while they’re on the call*


Here’s a breakdown of what that might look like in practice:


Action When it happens Example caller inquiry What the AI does


Answer Customer asks a routine question What time do you close on Saturdays? Replies with the answer


Capture Caller needs a human follow-up My water heater is leaking. Can someone come out? Collects the details you specify and summarizes them for your team


Transfer Caller needs human support I have a question about my invoice. Transfers the call to a person or department


Act Customer makes a request Can I book an appointment? Texts the caller a booking link while they're on the phone


**To perform SMS actions from your business phone number, you’ll need to enroll in*[A2P 10DLC](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a2p-10dlc/) *.*


##


What an AI receptionist can do


Here’s how an automated phone answering service can act as a virtual employee:


- **24/7 answering with custom greetings.** It’s always available to answer the phone.
- **Knowledge base answers.** With a good knowledge base, it answers routine questions about your hours, location, and services.
- **Message capture with fields you define.** It captures a caller’s name, email, and reason for calling.
- **Call transfer to a person or inbox.** It transfers calls to the number you’ve designated to receive them.
- **Mid-call SMS.** It sends text messages to callers while they’re still on the phone. That way, they can look at addresses, read about services, or book calls while they still have access to the agent.
- **Call recording and transcription.** It creates records of every AI-handled call and provides summaries and transcripts for immediate context.
- **Multiple language support.**[AI agents like Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) can switch languages during calls based on caller preference.
- **Follows an existing call flow.** It handles calls whenever you want it to — during weekends, the holidays, or your lunch break.
- [SMS lead capture](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/sona-sms) **.** Agents like Sona can reply to texts from new leads and follow up by text for missed calls.


Learn more about[how to set up an AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-set-up-ai-receptionist/) .


##


What an AI receptionist can’t do


[Automated receptionists](https://www.quo.com/blog/automated-receptionist/) can do a lot for your business, but they also have limitations.


You can’t use an AI receptionist to reliably handle:


- **Complex or unusual requests.** If your AI receptionist encounters a question it can’t answer, it will forward the caller to a human team member. That’s a good thing, since it won’t hallucinate or make up incorrect info. But it does mean someone still needs to be reachable at your business.
- **Emotional or high-stakes calls.** An upset customer wants to talk to a person, not artificial intelligence. And around[61% have yelled at automation](https://go.parloa.com/consumer-patience-index) to get routed to a human faster. Case in point: you can’t rely on AI to navigate complex emotional conversations.
- **Anything outside the knowledge base.** AI receptionists are only as good as the knowledge base you use to train them. The amount of time you spend setting up workflows and instructions — as well as the tool’s knowledge base — will impact its effectiveness.
- **Direct calendar booking.** Many AI receptionists, including Quo, text a booking link rather than booking directly into your calendar. But some competitors *do* book directly to your Outlook or Google Calendar. You need to check with your provider if that’s a make-or-break for your business.
- **Regulated data.** Personal healthcare information and similar categories are subject to HIPAA laws. But not all AI receptionists offer HIPAA compliance, especially if you’re working with CRM integrations or using it to qualify leads.
- **Outbound calls.** Some AI receptionists, like Sona, can only answer inbound calls or send SMS follow-ups for inbound events, like a missed call or text. If you want to build an AI tool that automates outbound follow-ups, you’ll need to look for a dedicated tool.


##


Is an AI receptionist worth it?


An AI receptionist *may* be worth it for your business if:


- A significant number of calls are going to voicemail while you work or after hours
- You get the same handful of questions all day
- You want to prevent missed calls and missed revenue


Quo’s Sona is one of the[best answering services](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-ai-phone-answering-services/) for these situations, and customers say the same:


*“We’ve been using Sona, and it’s been a huge help. It answers calls, provides clear information the first time, and even redirects people when they call the wrong line, all without pulling a team member away from their work.”* — Brandon Ingram, Sales and Operations Manager, Environment Control


That said, an AI receptionist *may not* be worth it if:


- Your call volume is low enough that you catch most calls
- Almost every call is complicated, emotional, or high-value


In either case, a live receptionist is the better choice.

##


FAQs


**What does an AI receptionist cost?**


Most AI receptionists charge $25 to $250+ per month for a set number of bundled minutes or calls. Quo includes 10 Sona-handled calls per month on every plan. For the full breakdown, see[what a virtual receptionist costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/virtual-receptionist-cost/) .


**Is an AI receptionist legit?**


Yes, most AI receptionists are legit. The main thing to watch for is how to escalate calls to humans, since that’s where callers can get frustrated. Make sure your virtual assistant knows how to forward calls to humans if it can’t solve a problem or doesn’t understand caller intent.


**Can an AI receptionist book appointments?**


Some AI voice agents like[Ruby](https://www.quo.com/blog/ruby-receptionist-alternatives/) book appointments directly into your calendar, but this requires a premium add-on. Other systems, like Sona, text callers a booking link so they can book the appointment themselves. This is included for free on every Sona tier.


**Will callers know they are talking to AI?**


Yes, most AI virtual receptionists announce that they’re not a real person. This helps set expectations and prevent callers from getting frustrated. If you train your AI to follow your brand voice and use natural conversation, customers may find it easier to trust the tool.


**What happens when the AI can’t answer a question?**


Every AI answering service provider is different. With Sona, you can set criteria so the AI knows when to escalate a call. It then lets the caller know they’re being transferred and routes the call to your team. Other services, like[Smith.ai](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-alternatives/) or Abby Connect, let you escalate calls to their live agents for an additional fee.
